_contract: Authored by Tasklet 2026-08-15. Sources: boston/FLEET-ECONOMICS-BOSTON.md + boston/TRACKER-SNAPSHOT-2026-08-15.md. Per module: 'copy' renders VERBATIM; 'data' is structured values Grok formats. Underscore-prefixed fields are non-renderable guard notes — never reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing (fail closed). This is fleet financing only — the equity/fundraise/defense/Gulf content firewalls in FLEET-INVESTORS-BRIEF.md §5 apply in full. Every economic figure renders WITH its assumption label; ranges only, no point estimates. D6 LOCKED: anchor-plus-fill leads; seat-band fill is upside, never headline.

copy.headline: Own the fleet behind Boston's water commuter network.
copy.subline: Anchor revenue is contracted before capital deploys. Seat-band fill is upside on top — never the base case.

roles: Fleet Investor — owns/finances the Boston fleet (workboat-grade N45s; N30 where corridor-appropriate).
Operator — runs the service (crewing, operations); existing Boston operators are natural candidates. No operator is committed.
Navier — supplies vessels, software, and the network platform.
Employers — contract committed seats, the revenue backbone.
Public Partners — grant landings at existing piers and marina berths; no terminal construction.
copy.trigger: Corridors launch only at 60–80 committed seats. Capital deploys behind committed demand, not ahead of it.

copy.redeployability: A vessel is a network asset, not stranded in one market: the 7-city network is the residual-value story.

data.inherit: unchanged (Decision D3 — same corridor map as the employer site)

copy.trigger_explainer: Each corridor activates only when 60–80 seats are committed. Launch timing honesty: end-2027 earliest.

demand_pool.standing_label: Indicative of demand potential along these corridors — not commitments or commercial relationships.

data.capture_assumption: 3.0% of on-site headcount (tracker's own stated input)
honesty_notes: 5 of 10 tracked nodes have zero sourced headcount — pools understate.
BOS-5 carries the largest sourced pool (North Station + Encore) but is a phase-3 line with zero launch-phase vessels — that demand is not actionable at launch under current phasing.

copy.rules: Named employers appear only as indicative demand potential under the standing label — never as customers, partners, or LOI signatories. Blank tracker cells stay blank.

pnl.structure: anchor_first (D6 LOCKED): anchor contract line → fill upside band → opex → network share → indicative payback range

anchor_line.label: Anchor-tenant block, indicative (program canon reference). No Boston anchor commitment is sourced or confirmed.

fill_upside_band.label: Seat-band fill, shown as upside only — program band $650–1,200/seat-month; Boston-specific pricing TBD; not a city quote.
fill_upside_band.honesty_note: Standalone per-seat vessel economics do not pencil under conservative-to-mid assumptions (net negative monthly; upside case ~80-year payback). Shown for transparency, never as headline economics. Combined anchor-plus-fill was not modeled this pass — fill is qualitative upside on top of the anchor block.

lines.label: Canon 4.1 kWh/nm @ $0.30/kWh × route distance × 1–2 round trips/day × 22 days/month. Electric-operation assumption; hybrid day-1 vessels may run higher.
N45 NOT validated — N30 canon ($65K/yr) floor, $100K/yr stated ceiling assumption, ÷12.
Placeholder benchmark, not canon, not validated — 2-crew workboat norm, $75–95/hr combined, 5–7 op hrs/day, 22 days/month.
Placeholder, weak basis — hull/liability ~1.5–3%/yr of insured value + illustrative berth fee loosely anchored to one documented commercial rate; not a Navier-specific quote.

network_share.value: 10% of gross revenue, off the top
network_share.label: canon

payback_summary.seat_conservative: not cash-flow positive at single-vessel scale
payback_summary.seat_mid: not cash-flow positive at single-vessel scale
payback_summary.seat_upside: ~80 years — not an attractive standalone payback
payback_summary.label: Indicative ranges only, conservative default. Upside comes from more corridors activating, not from inflating per-corridor assumptions.

speed_relief_upside_row.label: With authority speed-rule relief (precedent: Stockholm Candela P-12 exemption)
speed_relief_upside_row.note: Not quantified for Boston this pass — renders as a labeled upside row without numbers. Never blended into base or mid cases; base economics respect posted limits.

launch.label: Minimum viable launch fleet — 1–2 vessels per phase-1 line, sized to trigger-scale AM/PM peak sailings, not continuous headway. Derived, not published. No spares margin included.

full_build.label: 60-minute continuous-headway ceiling — an illustrative capacity-ceiling planning tool, not a timetable or day-1 requirement. Dwell/turnaround/headway are illustrative assumptions.

data.spares_note: No maintenance-reserve/spare vessel included in any count; a real fleet plan typically adds ~10–15% spares capacity (not computed this pass).

cards.title: Demand-gated launch
cards.body: Corridors launch only at 60–80 committed seats — capital deploys behind committed demand, not ahead of it.

cards.title: Redeployable network asset
cards.body: Workboat-grade N45s redeploy across the 7-city network; a vessel is not stranded in one market.

cards.title: Navier platform continuity
cards.body: Vessels, software, demand generation, and the network platform stay with Navier across operators and cities.

cards.title: Phased fleet growth
cards.body: Fleet scales with corridor activation — launch fleet first, growth tranches only as corridors hit trigger.

copy.body: Summary economics with every assumption stated, conservative default, ranges not points — and a conversation.
